title: Safely embedding lesson data
tldr: The renderer embeds lesson JSON in an HTML page.
Escaping special characters keeps lesson text from ending its script element.

snippets.explanation: JSON serialization alone does not protect an HTML script boundary. Escaping angle brackets keeps user-provided text inside the JSON payload.

challenges.title: Prove a snippet cannot inject HTML
challenges.task: Add a renderer test with a code snippet containing a closing script tag followed by an HTML element. Verify that the payload survives as text without creating an extra element.
hints: Look at the existing test for a title containing a closing script tag.
Read the generated lesson-data element and parse its JSON. Compare the recovered snippet with the original.
checks: The recovered code exactly matches the input.
The payload does not create another script or HTML element.
The existing renderer tests still pass.
challenges.solution: Render a lesson whose snippets[0].code contains . Parse the generated HTML, assert that only the two template script elements exist and no img element was created, then parse lesson-data and compare the code with the original string. The embed function escapes the HTML delimiters while JSON.parse restores the original text.
